response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Fix off-by-one in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11-14
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29-38

Explanation:
`Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` reports one page too many whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. For example, 50 members with a limit of 50 gives `totalPages = 2`.

The consequences:
- The UI shows "1/2".
- `showingLast` is false on the real last page.
- Clicking "next" sets `offset = min(50, 50) = 50` and loads an empty page that is labelled "2/2".

Proposed fix:
~~~js
totalPages: function() {
  if (this.get("user_count") == 0) { return 0; }
  return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));
}.property("limit", "user_count"),
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security
Title: Validate and bound `limit`/`offset` on the public members endpoint

Affected:
- app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26

Explanation:
`limit` and `offset` come straight from the request with only `to_i` applied. This causes two problems on this public, non-admin endpoint:
- **Unbounded size:** any visitor can request `limit=10000000` and force a huge query plus serialization, which is a cheap DoS vector.
- **Server errors:** negative values (`limit=-1` or `offset=-5`) make PostgreSQL raise "LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative", which returns a 500.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
limit  = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min
offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 users

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6
- app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26

Explanation:
Previously, non-automatic groups returned all their members. The endpoint now always paginates with a default of 50.

The public `group/members` template iterates `members` but has no pagination controls. Any group with more than 50 members therefore only ever shows the first 50, with no way to see the rest.

Fix: add next/previous controls (or infinite loading) to the public members page, reusing `offset`/`limit` on the model.

Proposed fix:
~~~
Add pagination actions to the group-members controller (mirroring admin-group next/previous) and render controls in group/members.hbs.
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Maintainability
Title: Breaking change to `/groups/:id/members` response shape and `findMembers` contract

Affected:
- app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20-38

Explanation:
There are two contract changes here:
- **Endpoint shape:** it previously returned a bare JSON array and now returns `{members, meta}`.
- **`findMembers` behaviour:** it used to resolve to an array of users. It now resolves to `undefined` and mutates the model instead. When `name` is empty it returns `undefined` rather than a promise.

Any other caller that does `group.findMembers().then(function(members){...})` will break. That includes other routes, plugins, or API consumers I cannot see in this diff, and the empty-name case would throw "cannot read property 'then' of undefined". The impact depends on callers outside the diff, so I am rating this medium.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
findMembers: function() {
  if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]); }
  ...
  }).then(function(result) {
    var members = result.members.map(function(m) { return Discourse.User.create(m); });
    self.setProperties({ ..., members: members });
    return members;
  });
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Adding an already-present member may raise and return a 500

Affected:
- app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75

Explanation:
`group.add(user)` is called for every username, with no check for existing membership. If `group.add` appends to `users` and `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, re-adding an existing member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. That aborts the whole request with a 500 and can leave the batch partially applied.

This depends on the `Group#add` implementation and the indexes, which are not shown in the diff.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
existing = group.user_ids.to_set
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
  user = User.find_by_username(username.strip)
  group.add(user) if user && !existing.include?(user.id)
end
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: No error handling or input reset after add/remove member

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:51-65
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60

Explanation:
`addMembers` and `removeMember` ignore rejected promises. For example, a 422 for an automatic group or a server error gives the admin no feedback. The usernames input is also never cleared after a successful add (the TODO acknowledges this), so pressing "Add" again re-submits the same users. Combined with issue 5, that resubmission could cause errors.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
addMembers: function() {
  var self = this;
  if (Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))) { return; }
  this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")).then(function() {
    self.set("usernames", null);
  }, function() {
    bootbox.alert(I18n.t("generic_error"));
  });
},
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Specs rely on a hard-coded group id and use the wrong HTTP verb

Affected:
- spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:51-58
- spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:93-96
- spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:114-117

Explanation:
- **Hard-coded id:** several tests assume `Group.find(1)` exists and is automatic (the seeded "everyone" group). That is brittle and depends on seed data and sequence state.
- **Wrong verb:** the `remove_member` automatic-group test uses `xhr :put` even though the route is `DELETE`.

Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use the correct verb.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
it "cannot remove members from automatic groups" do
  group = Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)
  xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: 42
  response.status.should == 422
end
~~~

false_positives.candidate: limit and offset parameters on public members endpoint are not validated or bounded, allowing unbounded query sizes (DoS vector) and negative values causing PostgreSQL errors

Adding an already-present member may raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and return 500, potentially leaving batch partially applied
No error handling or input reset after add/remove member - rejected promises are ignored and usernames input is never cleared after successful add
Specs rely on hard-coded group id (Group.find(1)) which is brittle and depends on seed data

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
